newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Women, children rally for peace in Tirana.
newsitem.headline: Women, children rally for peace in Tirana.

text.p: Several hundred people, many of them mothers with their children, demonstrated in central Tirana on Sunday to demand an end to violent unrest that has gripped Albania.

Waving flowers and chanting "peace, peace" they paraded round Skanderbeg square in bright sunlight calling for Albanians to unite to combat the spree of looting and shooting that has come close to tearing the Balkan country apart.
Some called out the name of Bashkim Fino, prime minister in a national unity government that is attempting to restore order in Albania.
Albania came close to all-out anarchy earlier this month after the collapse of shady pyramid investment schemes in which thousands of families lost their savings.
Angry Albanians then raided army barracks and looted thousands of weapons. They took over a string of towns, mostly in in the south of the country, and demanded that President Sali Berisha resign.
More than 100 people have died and many more have been wounded, mostly as a result of stray bullets.
Students whose campus near Tirana was wrecked by looters appealed for funds to help them rebuild it. People stepped forward to put money in a box on a makeshift table.
One of the organisers said the demonstration was a sign that people were sick of violence.
"We are mothers, women and sisters. We need peace and life. This is our message today," said one protester.
